elements.element: Vendor has an express duty to defend Customer and its affiliates.
elements.evidence: Retained Section 14.1: "RevMed shall indemnify, defend and hold harmless Sanofi, its Affiliates and their respective officers, directors, agents and employees (\"Sanofi Indemnitees\")" — express defend obligation running to Customer and its Affiliates.

elements.element: Vendor indemnifies Customer and its affiliates against third-party claims.
elements.evidence: Section 14.1 covers "any Third Party Claims and Losses arising therefrom under or related to this Agreement" in favour of the Sanofi Indemnitees (Sanofi and its Affiliates); "Third Party Claims" and "Losses" are both defined terms (1.126, 1.60).

elements.element: Vendor indemnity covers claims that Services or Deliverables infringe intellectual property rights.
elements.evidence: New limb: "(d) the infringement or misappropriation of any intellectual property right of a Third Party by the RevMed Licensed Technology or by Sanofi's exercise of the licenses granted to it under this Agreement". There are no "Services" or "Deliverables" in this collaboration/licence structure; the licensed technology and Customer's exercise of the licences are the correct analogues, so the substance of the element is delivered notwithstanding the keyword-based regex ("vendor indemnity for IP infringement present": false) which searched for services/deliverables wording.

elements.element: Vendor indemnity covers Vendor's breach of applicable law.
elements.evidence: Retained 14.1(c) indemnifies "the material breach by RevMed of any of its obligations pursuant to this Agreement", and Section 13.4(b) makes compliance "in all material respects with all Applicable Law" an express obligation, so material non-compliance with law in performance is within the indemnity. Note the coverage is indirect and doubly qualified by materiality (13.4(b) "in all material respects" plus 14.1(c) "material breach") and is limited to law-breaking in Research, Development, Manufacture, Commercialization and performance of the Agreement.

elements.element: Vendor indemnity covers a data breach caused by Vendor.
elements.evidence: New limb: "(e) any unauthorized access to, or disclosure of, Sanofi's Confidential Information or other Sanofi data caused by RevMed" — covers all categories of Customer data, not merely named types.

elements.element: Vendor indemnity covers Vendor's gross negligence and wilful misconduct.
elements.evidence: Retained 14.1(a): "the negligence, recklessness or willful misconduct of any of the RevMed Indemnitees" — simple negligence subsumes gross negligence, and wilful misconduct is express.

elements.element: The indemnification procedure requires notice of a claim.
elements.evidence: Section 14.3(a): "The Indemnified Party will give the indemnifying Party ... prompt written notice (an \"Indemnification Claim Notice\") of any Losses ... upon which such Indemnified Party intends to base a request for indemnification under Section 14.1 or Section 14.2".

elements.element: The indemnification procedure allocates control of the defence.
elements.evidence: Section 14.3(b) Control of Defense: "At its option, the Indemnifying Party may assume the defense of any Third Party Claim ... by giving written notice ... within [***]", with counsel selection and consequences of assumption.

elements.element: The indemnification procedure requires reasonable cooperation.
elements.evidence: Section 14.3(e) Cooperation: "the Indemnified Party will, and will cause each other Indemnitee to, cooperate in the defense thereof and will furnish such records, information and testimony ... as may be reasonably requested", with Indemnifying Party reimbursement of out-of-pocket costs.

elements.element: Customer indemnity is limited to Customer-provided content and Customer's breach of law.
elements.evidence: Section 14.2 as redlined reads only: "(a) any content, data or materials provided by Sanofi to RevMed under this Agreement; or (b) Sanofi's breach of Applicable Law; (c) [Intentionally omitted.] (d) [Intentionally omitted.]" — the former Research/Development/Manufacture/Commercialization, negligence and breach limbs are removed.

elements.element: Vendor indemnifies Customer against third-party intellectual-property claims.
elements.evidence: New 14.1(d) covers Third Party infringement/misappropriation claims against the licensed technology and Customer's exercise of the licences.

elements.element: The IP indemnity may exclude infringement caused by Customer modifications.
elements.evidence: Permissive element: no Customer-modification exclusion is added, which is more favourable to Customer than the fallback tolerates, so the condition does not bite.

elements.element: The IP indemnity may exclude infringement caused by Customer combinations.
elements.evidence: Permissive element: no combination exclusion is added; the retained carve-outs are limited to Sanofi's negligence/wilful misconduct and Sanofi's breaches, so the element's condition does not apply.

elements.element: The IP indemnity may exclude infringement caused by Customer specifications.
elements.evidence: Permissive element: no Customer-specification exclusion is added; nothing to fail.

elements.element: Vendor must procure continued use, modify, or replace the infringing item.
elements.evidence: No procure/modify/replace remedy appears anywhere in the rendered Section 14 or elsewhere in the cited text; Section 10.7 only obliges the parties to negotiate Third Party licences.

elements.element: Vendor must refund applicable fees if procure, modify, or replace remedies are unavailable.
elements.evidence: No refund mechanic is inserted or retained.

elements.element: Vendor's indemnity is subject to a super-cap of three times annual fees.
elements.evidence: No 3x annual-fees super-cap is proposed; the drafter expressly declines it (indemnity claims remain uncapped under Section 14.5).

elements.element: Vendor's indemnity is subject to a super-cap of three times annual fees.
elements.evidence: Not a preferred-level requirement; no cap element applies at the preferred position and the uncapped indemnity preserved by Section 14.5 is Customer-favourable.

reasons: Preferred checklist is complete on the operative language: the two inserted limbs (IP infringement/misappropriation and unauthorised access/disclosure of Sanofi data) close the only real gaps, and the retained 14.1(a)/(c) plus the Section 14.3 notice, control-of-defence and cooperation machinery supply the remaining elements.

The deterministic check "vendor indemnity for IP infringement present: false" is a wording-level false negative: it appears to look for "Services"/"Deliverables" infringement language, which does not exist in this collaborative research/licence agreement. Substantively, new 14.1(d) is a full Vendor IP indemnity covering both the RevMed Licensed Technology and Sanofi's exercise of the granted licences.

Fallback level is deliberately not taken and is incomplete (no procure/modify/replace, no refund, no 3x cap). That is acceptable because the preferred level is complete, and the rationale for declining the super-cap (it would introduce a cap on a presently uncapped indemnity and "annual fees" has no analogue in a milestone/royalty structure) is sound.

Minimality holds: the edits are confined to adding limbs (d) and (e), conforming the "(a) through (e)" cross-reference, and rewriting Section 14.2 to the two permitted limbs. No survival tails, expense allocations, extra damages categories or boilerplate were added, and favourable retained language (uncapped indemnity via 14.5; the pro-Customer 14.1 carve-out structure) is preserved.

Verify that "RevMed Licensed Technology" is the exact defined term used in the Agreement (it is not among the resolved definitions supplied). If the defined term is, e.g., "RevMed Technology" or "RevMed Licensed Patents and RevMed Know-How", limb (d) will contain an undefined term and must be conformed.

Housekeeping on Section 14.2: with (c) and (d) marked "[Intentionally omitted.]", the list punctuation/conjunction should be conformed (limb (a) should not end with "or" running into an omitted tail), and any closing "except in each case ((a) through (d))" flush paragraph or other cross-reference to 14.2(c)-(d) elsewhere in the Agreement or the Ancillary Agreements (Profit/Loss Share, Co-Promotion) should be checked so no dangling reference survives.

Commercial flag for the negotiator, not a checklist defect: deleting former 14.2(a)/(b) removes Sanofi's indemnity for its own Development/Commercialization activities and its own negligence. That narrowing is exactly what the preferred element requires, but expect strong pushback in a collaboration where Sanofi commercialises the Product; RevMed's 14.1 carve-out (i) for Sanofi negligence still protects RevMed on that axis.

Optional hardening: because limbs are already being inserted, consider an express "(f) RevMed's breach of Applicable Law" limb. Breach of law is currently reached only indirectly through 14.1(c) "material breach ... of its obligations" read with the Section 13.4(b) "in all material respects" compliance covenant, so non-material or non-performance-related legal breaches sit outside the indemnity.

Cross-check Section 10.7 (obligation to negotiate Third Party licences) and any associated cost allocation against new 14.1(d) so the two do not read as competing allocations of Third Party licence cost; the 14.1 "except ... (iii) any breach by Sanofi of its obligations" tail could otherwise be argued to bite where Sanofi has not pursued a 10.7 licence.
